introduction: Himalayan rivers are 'perennial', meaning they have water throughout the year. This is because they receive water from both monsoon rainfall and the melting of Himalayan glaciers. The three major Himalayan river systems are the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra.

core_concepts.title: Ganga River System
core_concepts.description: It is the longest river in India (2525 km) and forms the largest river basin. It originates from the Gangotri Glacier (Gomukh) in Uttarakhand as the 'Bhagirathi' and ultimately drains into the Bay of Bengal.

core_concepts.title: Indus River System
core_concepts.description: It originates from the 'Bokhar Chu' glacier near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet. It flows northwest through the Ladakh region of India, enters Pakistan, and finally drains into the Arabian Sea.

core_concepts.title: Brahmaputra River System
core_concepts.description: It originates from the 'Chemayungdung' glacier near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet. It flows parallel to the Himalayas in Tibet, enters India through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, and flows into Bangladesh.

core_concepts.title: Sundarban Delta
core_concepts.description: Before flowing into the Bay of Bengal, the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers combine to form the Sundarban Delta, which is the largest and fastest-growing river delta in the world.

important_entities.name: National River
important_entities.significance: The Ganga was declared the 'National River' of India in 2008. Its water contains viruses called 'Bacteriophages' that destroy harmful bacteria, preventing the water from spoiling easily.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common mistake is thinking the Brahmaputra enters India through Assam. It actually takes a U-turn near the Namcha Barwa peak and enters India through 'Arunachal Pradesh', where it is first called the 'Dihang' river.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The total length of the Ganga River is exactly 2525 kilometers, making it very easy to memorize for objective exams.

exam_strategy_tips: The origins of these rivers are highly tested: Ganga (Gangotri), Indus (Mansarovar/Bokhar Chu), and Brahmaputra (Mansarovar/Chemayungdung).
Remember that the Brahmaputra is the largest river in India by 'volume of water', but the Ganga is the 'longest' river within India's borders.
